description: Prepared with apples, rye flour, and cornmeal.
steps: Peel the apples, remove the seeds, and slice them.

steps: Chop two medium onions finely and brown them with butter in a pan.
Cut the veal meat into cubes, dust with flour, add to the browned onions, salt and add paprika to taste.

Stew on low heat until the meat is tender.

title: Pieczeń Barania po Myśliwsku (Lamb Roast Hunter Style)
description: Prepared with lamb, vegetables, and vinegar.
steps: Marinate lamb loin for four days, adding to the marinade in addition to vegetables, vinegar and spices, also some juniper berries.
After removing from the marinade, roast the roast as usual, slice into thin slices, arrange on a serving platter and pour with the following sauce:

Finely chop one onion, one small carrot, a piece of ham, add a bay leaf, several peppercorns and a celery stalk; brown all this in butter, then add two tablespoons vinegar, some broth and braise on low heat until tender.
Then strain through a sieve, pour into the sauce that remained on the roasting pan from the lamb roast and boil once more.
This sauce is called sharp; to have a wild sauce, a few tablespoons of sour cream should be added to it.

description: Prepared with veal, bread or bread crumbs, and bacon.

ingredients.name: piece of veal from the leg

steps: Take a piece of veal from the leg and remove the bone.

Soak one cup of grated bread or bread crumbs in a little water, add one tablespoon of butter, a quarter teaspoon of salt, some pepper and a bit of powdered thyme. Mix into a paste and fill with this stuffing the place where the bone was.
Roll the meat and tie with twine. Rub the top with salt, pepper and flour.
Place in a roasting pan, put a couple of bacon slices on top, add water and roast in a moderately hot oven.
Baste frequently to avoid burning; for this purpose the meat can also be covered with paper.
Roast for about two hours.

description: Prepared with veal, béchamel, and parmesan cheese.
steps: Roast the meat as usual. When it is almost done, cut it deeply and interlard with béchamel sauce mixed with Parmesan.

To prepare the béchamel: Take a quarter pound of young butter, bring to a boil with one tablespoon flour, mix in a half cup of sour cream, cook down to half.
Then season with three egg yolks beaten previously with one tablespoon of cold sour cream, and then add a quarter pound of grated Parmesan.

title: Pieczeń Cielęca Zawijana (Rolled Veal Roast)
description: Prepared with veal, lemon, and bacon.
steps: Butterfly the small quarter of veal lengthwise so the bones are loosened. After removing the bones, pound the meat well and season with salt and a bit of nutmeg.
Sprinkle inside with lemon, using one large or one and a half medium lemons. Over the lemon, lay finely sliced young bacon to cover the entire inner surface.
Roll tightly into a log and tie with twine.
Place the rolled roast in a salad bowl or dish, sprinkle with good vinegar and place in a cold pantry for two days. Every day it should be turned several times.
After two days, remove from the dish, salt well and let it rest in salt for about three hours.
Then place on a roasting pan and bake in a moderately hot oven, basting frequently with butter. At the end of roasting, season with one tablespoon of good sour cream to form a creamy sauce.
Serve sliced.

title: Puree z Grochu (Pea Puree)
description: Prepared with peas, onion, and cream.
steps: Pour one quart of ordinary dried peas into a pan, cover with soft water and bring to a boil. After skimming, drain the water, rinse the peas in fresh water and then cover with another hot water and cook until completely soft.
During cooking add one tablespoon of butter, one blanched onion and a little parsley.
When the peas are well cooked, mash them with a roller, then press through a fine sieve; if too thick, add some hot water.

Place one tablespoon of good butter in a pan and brown lightly with a quarter tablespoon of flour, and when it thickens, dilute with one cup of sweet cream, add to the pressed peas, mix well, heat on hot fire and serve.

description: A soup made with broth or beef bones or veal, vegetables, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: ordinary broth from beef bones, veal, or offal
ingredients.sourceText: ordinary broth from beef bones, veal, or offal

steps: Cook ordinary broth, which may be made from beef bones, veal, or offal.
After the broth is cooked and vegetables added in whole form, take two large cauliflowers, clean them, place in a pot, cover with cold water, salt, and bring to a boil once, then drain the water.
Break the cauliflowers into pieces and place in the broth, cooking until completely tender.
Remove all the vegetables from the broth.
Press the broth together with the cauliflower through a sieve or colander, then pour back into the pot and bring to a boil.
Brown a spoon of flour with a spoon of butter and thicken the boiling soup with this mixture.
Beat two egg yolks well with a spoon of cold water, pour into a serving bowl and onto this slowly pour the hot soup, stirring constantly with a spoon.
This soup is usually served with small pastries or croutons with cheese.

title: Puree z Kartofli (Potato Puree)
description: Prepared with potatoes, water, and milk.
steps: Peel and cook mealy potatoes in salted water
Cover the potatoes with cold water, never hot
After cooking drain the water and place the potatoes on the heat for a few minutes to dry
Then rub them to a paste
For each quart of such potatoes heat one cup of milk with salt and one tablespoon of butter
When the milk is hot, but should not boil, pour it over the potatoes and beat strongly with a spoon for at least three minutes until the potatoes become well white
Then serve at table

The method above is American; the European method differs in that instead of milk sour cream is used, not heated, and the pot with potatoes during beating is placed in another pot filled with hot water

steps: Select a young and fat turkey weighing ten to twelve pounds
After plucking, singe over a sheet of lit paper, holding the turkey carefully to avoid tearing the innards
Wash carefully in four waters; add one teaspoon of baking soda to the third water
Dry thoroughly both inside and outside, then rub the inside with a little salt
Roast two dozen chestnuts and peel them

Fry five small pork sausages in butter until half cooked; add one cup of grated bread or white bread, one large spoon of butter, salt and pepper to taste and the remaining whole chestnuts, stuff the turkey body with this filling and sew it shut with strong twine
Tie the legs and wings to the body; brush with butter and wipe with salt and pepper, then coat with flour
Place in a roasting pan and cover with thin slices of smoked bacon; place in a moderately hot oven
Roast for twenty minutes per pound of turkey, so for a twelve-pound turkey roast for four hours
During roasting, frequently baste and turn so that it browns evenly on all sides
Cook the giblets separately in salted water, then chop very finely and add to the sauce remaining in the pan after removing the turkey

steps: Cut the prepared and cleaned piglet lengthwise along the belly, discard the head and legs.
Remove from the bones and lay the skin on the table, skin side down.
Scrape all meat from the bones and head, chop finely, and mix with {{source-2}}.
Add the chopped liver of the piglet.
Season with salt, pepper, and a small amount of nutmeg flower.
Fry this mixture for half an hour in young pork fat on low heat, being careful not to brown the fat.
Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Add two small bread rolls (moistened and squeezed of water), three well-beaten whole eggs, and mix everything thoroughly.
Pass through a fine sieve.
Spread this farce on the laid out piglet.
Layer with slices of cooked ham with fat, or cooked young pork fat.
Layer with hard-boiled eggs, sliced.
Add another layer of farce.
Roll up, sew closed, wrap in a cloth, and cook in salted water with vinegar and mixed vegetables for two hours.
Remove from heat and cool slightly, then remove and press down with a board or stone to flatten, and cool completely.
When completely cold, slice and serve with vinegar and oil.
Note: If storing the roulade for longer during summer, do not add eggs or ham.
The remaining sauce in the pot should be clarified with egg whites, reheated, strained through cloth and cooled; this aspic is used to coat the sliced roulade.

title: Rosół (Beef Broth)
description: A soup made with beef or broth, leeks, and carrots.

ingredients.name: half pound beef per person, or one pound per person for a stronger broth

steps: Do not rinse the meat, as this removes significant nutrients. Instead, immediately pour water over it in a pot, preferably soft water, and simmer without skimming for three and a half to four hours. Cook over low heat, pouring in enough water at the start so that you do not need to add more during cooking, as this would diminish the quality of the broth. When cooking on very low heat, half a quart of water per person is sufficient. After the broth has cooked for about an hour and the foam stops appearing, pour in a spoonful of cold water, which will cause fat to rise to the surface. Skim this fat with a spoon. Then add whatever vegetables are available: parsley with roots, leeks, carrots, and onion. The onion can first be roasted on a sheet in the oven, which enhances the flavor of the broth. Before serving, let it rest off the heat for ten minutes, skim off the remaining fat, then strain through a sieve into a serving bowl, in which a little finely chopped parsley is placed.
